```{r}
library(rsample)
library(textstem)
library(sparsesvd)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(modelr)
library(Matrix)
library(glmnet)
```


This code is similar to in class activity "multinomial logistic regression":
```{r}
set.seed(2026)

source("../scripts/preprocessing-primary.R")
# The nlp_fn() function is basically doing tokenization, DTM then TF-IDF. Now the text is translated into numbers.

# there was an error where I had 1712 labels, but only 1580 rows of data. nlp_fn() dropped 132 pages probably because there were no valid words left to make a TF-IDF score.
# it seems the activity already had a "claims-multi-tfidf.csv" that did nlp_fn() on the data before splitting the data.
full_dtm <- nlp_fn(claims_clean)

# instead of splitting, I need to make sure I am testing on the same pages as Khio, 
#partitions <- initial_split(full_dtm, prop = .8)
#train_dtm <- training(partitions)
#test_dtm  <- testing(partitions)
# Loaded the validation IDs from 
val_ids <- readRDS("C:../data/val-ids.rds")

# Instead of initial_split(), split based on the same .id
test_dtm  <- filter(full_dtm, .id %in% val_ids)
train_dtm <- filter(full_dtm, !(.id %in% val_ids))

train_labels <- select(train_dtm, .id, bclass) %>%
  left_join(select(claims_clean, .id, mclass), by = ".id")
# need to save mclass because nlp_fn() doesn't save it.
# but using train_dtm, so need to get it from clean data
test_labels <- select(test_dtm, .id, bclass) %>%
  left_join(select(claims_clean, .id, mclass), by = ".id")
# used to check predictions
# had to left join by .id to get mclass in the joined table.
```


PCA / Projection
```{r}
# need to (PCA) project test data onto PCs, class activity uses reproject_fn(), a function created for this class activity.
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pstat197/pstat197a/main/materials/activities/data/projection-functions.R")

train_predictors <- select(train_dtm, -.id, -bclass)
test_predictors  <- select(test_dtm, -.id, -bclass)
# had to remove .id and bclass b/c projection_fn() can only handle numeric columns. But had to remove after creating the labels.

# projection_fn() is the PCA function
proj_out <- projection_fn(.dtm = train_predictors, .prop = .8)
train_dtm_projected <- proj_out$data
# reproject_fn() was also used in the activity for test projection
test_dtm_projected <- reproject_fn(.dtm = test_predictors, proj_out)

proj_out$n_pc
```


Train and Test data frames
```{r}
train <- train_labels %>%
  transmute(bclass = factor(bclass),
            mclass = factor(mclass)) %>%
  bind_cols(train_dtm_projected)

test <- test_labels %>%
  transmute(bclass = factor(bclass),
            mclass = factor(mclass)) %>%
  bind_cols(test_dtm_projected)
```


Binary Logistic Regression with Elastic Net
```{r}
# we use elastic net because glm() would overfit, glmnet() better handles correlated predictors and overfitting.
x_train <- as.matrix(select(train, -bclass, -mclass))
# glmnet() doesn't accept tibbles, so have to change it to a numeric matrix.
y_train_bin <- train$bclass

set.seed(2026)
# alpha = .1 b/c a more ridge regression is better when there are many predictors that have a small non-zero effect. (same as activity)
en_bin <- glmnet(x_train, y_train_bin, family = "binomial", alpha = .1)
# as seen in the activity, this uses cross validation. used to get lambda.min.
cv_bin <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train_bin, family = "binomial", alpha = .1)

# similar to x_train
x_test <- as.matrix(select(test, -bclass, -mclass))

pred_prob <- predict(en_bin, s = cv_bin$lambda.min,
                     newx = x_test, type = "response")

# store predictions in a data frame with true labels
pred_df_bin <- test_labels %>% 
  transmute(bclass = factor(bclass)) %>%
  bind_cols(pred = as.numeric(pred_prob)) %>%
  mutate(bclass.pred = factor(pred > .5, labels = levels(bclass)))
# so pred > .5 = "Relevant claim content", < .5 = N/A: No relevant content.

# define classification metric panel 
panel <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                    specificity, 
                    accuracy, 
                    roc_auc)

# compute test set accuracy
pred_df_bin %>% panel(truth = bclass, 
                      estimate = bclass.pred, 
                      pred, 
                      event_level = "second")
# sensitivity: all the pages that were relevant that the model knew was relevent
# specificity: all the pages that were irrelevant that the model knew was irrelevant.
# accuracy: how much the model predicted correct labels.
# roc_auc: how well the model is at separating the two classes (relevant and irrelevant)
```
accuracy = 0.7900943


Multiclass Logistic Regression with Elastic Net
```{r}
y_train_mult <- train$mclass

set.seed(2026)
# I chose alpha = .2 because there are now way more coefficients than training web pages
# so we are more at risk of overfitting. 
en_mult <- glmnet(x_train, y_train_mult, family = "multinomial", alpha = .2)
cv_mult <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train_mult, family = "multinomial", alpha = .2)

preds_multi <- predict(en_mult, s = cv_mult$lambda.min, 
                       newx = x_test, type = "response")

# this guarantees that as_tibble() receives a clean 2D matrix.
#as_tibble(preds_multi[, , 1])

# now we choose the most probable mclass value for each row
pred_class <- as_tibble(preds_multi[, , 1]) %>% 
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(-row, 
               names_to = "label", 
               values_to = "probability") %>% 
  group_by(row) %>% 
  slice_max(probability, n = 1) %>% 
  pull(label) %>%
  factor(levels = levels(train$mclass))
# needed to order by mclass 

# cross-tabulate predictions vs truth
pred_tbl <- table(test_labels$mclass, pred_class)
pred_tbl

# overall accuracy
sum(diag(pred_tbl)) / sum(pred_tbl)
# accuracy = .7334906

# classwise accuracy
diag(pred_tbl)/rowSums(pred_tbl)

# predictionwise accuracy rates
diag(pred_tbl)/colSums(pred_tbl)
```
overall accuracy = .7334906



Now we test the two models on claims-test.RData, where claims-test.RData has 929 webpages, but it has no labels.
Then we export a deployable copy of each model and a set of predictions from each model on the test data.
```{r}
load("../data/claims-test.RData")

# simialr to training data, we need to turn the raw unlabeled test webpages into clean text that basically resembles the training data.
# without this nlp_fn() would not work. 
# parse_data() is from preprocessing-primary.R, it uses parse_fn()
test_clean <- parse_data(claims_test) %>%
  select(.id, text_clean) %>%
  mutate(bclass = factor(NA))
# error where bclass was not found. 

# creates TF-IDF matrix
test_dtm_final <- nlp_fn(test_clean)


# I have to make sure that the data I trained my models have the same tokens as my test_clean (from claims-test.RData). 
missing_cols <- setdiff(colnames(train_predictors), colnames(test_dtm_final))
test_dtm_final[missing_cols] <- 0
# setdiff() is used to find the elements which are in train_predictors but not in test_dtm_final. it then outputs all the elements not in test_dtm_final.
# then for each token in missing_cols, fill each column with 0 if the column doesn't exist.
# For each token in missing_cols, assign 0 to every row of that column.
# now we remove extra tokens and reorder the test_dtm_final to match the train_predictors
extra_cols <- setdiff(colnames(test_dtm_final),
                      c(".id", "bclass", colnames(train_predictors)))
# setdiff() again but now finds tokens only in test_dtm_final
test_dtm_final <- select(test_dtm_final, -all_of(extra_cols))
# then we drop the extra tokens
test_dtm_final <- select(test_dtm_final, all_of(
  c(".id", "bclass", colnames(train_predictors))))
# reorders the tokens in the same order as train_predictors

# reproject onto the same proj_out, but have to remove .id and bclass
test_pcs_final <- reproject_fn(.dtm = test_dtm_final 
                               %>% select(-.id, -bclass), proj_out)
x_test_final <- as.matrix(test_pcs_final)
# glmnet() doesn't accept tibbles, so have to change it to a numeric matrix. just like x_test and x_train.


# Binary prediction (using binary elastic net model)
pred_prob_final <- predict(en_bin, s = cv_bin$lambda.min,
                           newx = x_test_final, type = "response") %>%
  as.numeric()
bclass_final <- factor(pred_prob_final > 0.5, 
                       labels = levels(train$bclass))
# pred > .5 = "Relevant claim content", < .5 = N/A: No relevant content. as prev seen.

# Multiclass prediction (using multiclass elastic net model)
pred_multi_final <- predict(en_mult, s = cv_mult$lambda.min,
                            newx = x_test_final, type = "response")

mclass_final <- as_tibble(pred_multi_final[, , 1]) %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(-row, names_to = "label", values_to = "probability") %>%
  group_by(row) %>%
  slice_max(probability, n = 1) %>%
  pull(label) %>%
  factor(levels = levels(train$mclass))

# It seems the claims-test.RData had 33 blank pages. 
# the blank pages were dropped by nlp_fn().
# the blank page should have been labled "N/A: No relevant content." 
# filter(test_clean, .id %in% dropped_ids)
pred_df <- test_clean %>%
  select(.id) %>%
  left_join(test_dtm_final %>%
              select(.id) %>%
              bind_cols(bclass.pred = bclass_final, 
                        mclass.pred = mclass_final), 
            by = ".id") %>%
# create a table with columns .id, bclass.pred and mclass.pred. with the NA values (the blank pages)
  mutate(bclass.pred = if_else(is.na(bclass.pred),
                               factor("N/A: No relevant content.", 
                                      levels = levels(bclass.pred)),
                               bclass.pred),
         mclass.pred = if_else(is.na(mclass.pred),
                               factor("N/A: No relevant content.", 
                                      levels = levels(mclass.pred)),
                               mclass.pred) )
# mutate the bclass.pred and mclass.pred columns, if NA return "N/A: No relevant content." (as a factor)
# otherwise return bclass.pred / mclass.pred
```



Save models
```{r}
# "Export a deployable copy of each model and a set of predictions from each model on the test data."
saveRDS(en_bin, "../results/glmnet_binary_model.rds")
saveRDS(en_mult, "../results/glmnet_multiclass_model.rds")
saveRDS(pred_df, "../results/glmnet_pred_df.rds")
```
